items.question_en: At constant pressure, equal amounts of heat are supplied to a monatomic gas and a diatomic gas separately. The ratio of the increases in internal energies of the two gases is

solution.approach: At constant pressure the increase in internal energy is the heat supplied times the ratio of specific heats, Cᵥ over Cₚ, which equals 1/γ for each gas.

steps.text: At constant pressure, the heat supplied and the rise in internal energy are related through the specific heats.
steps.equation: Q = nCₚΔT, ΔU = nCᵥΔT, so ΔU = Q × (Cᵥ/Cₚ) = Q/γ
steps.why_this_step: Only part of the heat supplied at constant pressure raises the internal energy; the rest goes into the work done as the gas expands.

steps.text: Write 1/γ for each gas using its known ratio of specific heats.
steps.equation: monatomic: γ = 5/3, so ΔU₁ = 3Q/5; diatomic: γ = 7/5, so ΔU₂ = 5Q/7

steps.text: Form the ratio, which does not depend on the amount of gas since the same Q is supplied to both.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the heat becomes internal energy for both gases as it would at constant volume, which wrongly gives an equal increase of 1:1.
